chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan, from Fadalah, from Husayn ibn Uthman, from Sama'ah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Witr prayer is three rak'ahs until the sun sets; when it sets, [then it is] four rak'ahs.

key_terms.الْوَتْرُ: Witr (odd-numbered prayer, typically performed at night)
key_terms.زَوَالِ الشَّمْسِ: Sunset (the time when the sun disappears below the horizon)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and timing for the Witr prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the variable structure of the Witr prayer within the Shia tradition, distinguishing between the pre-sunset period where it is performed as three rak'ahs and the post-sunset period where it expands to four. This distinction highlights the flexibility in the timing and composition of supererogatory prayers, reflecting the scholarly emphasis on aligning voluntary acts with the natural progression of the day. The hadith serves as a key reference in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* for understanding the practical application of night prayers in relation to the sunset transition.
